clue.text: One gem of a game

definitions.meaning: a diamond or other stone set on its own in a ring
a card game played by one person, also a peg-board game

explanation.surface: Someone praises a particularly fine game as a real gem.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a single mounted stone and a one-player game, so each definition is a dictionary sense.

clue.text: Promise to serve a hot stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook things together in a jumble, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A host promises to serve up a hot stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise or sworn vow is a synonym, as in taking an oath in court.

clue.text: Stylish lady needs it to succeed

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish, as in the in thing
her refers to a lady or woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman needs something in order to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone, as heir to their estate or title, is to come into what they leave.

clue.text: Skill is an essential in his work

definitions.text: Skill is an essential in his work

parts.note: art means skill or craft, as in the art of baking
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that skill is indispensable in a craftsman's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as the definition: a craftsperson is someone for whom skill is essential in their work.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker is one whose trade depends on craft skill, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: People in competition

definitions.meaning: a nation or ethnic group of people
a contest of speed, such as a sprint

explanation.surface: Some people taking part in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ethnic group of people and a speed contest, two separate dictionary senses.

clue.text: Basically a nest egg meant for use by friend

parts.note: a nest egg is a fund of savings put aside

indicators.note: the letters are put to new use, rearranged into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Essentially, savings intended to be used by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for use' is the anagram signal: the five letters of 'meant' are put to new use in a different order. 'by' only joins the friend to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at root or in essence, so the adverb is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Armies and legions deployed at his command

definitions.text: Armies and legions deployed at his command

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out and rearranged, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A supreme commander sends armies and legions into the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges the letters of ARMIES and LEGIONS; 'and' only joins them. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme military commander is the one at whose command whole armies are deployed.

clue.text: Exactly what is needed by bus passenger

definitions.meaning: an idiom for the perfect or ideal thing
read literally, a passenger on a bus needs a fare slip

explanation.surface: A bus passenger's essential item is just right.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely the right thing, and literally a bus traveller needs a fare slip.

clue.text: First-class fish often served with pork

parts.note: crack means excellent or first-rate, as in a crack shot
a ling is a long sea fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: A top-quality fish is often served alongside pork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'often served with pork' looks like it describes the fish, but it defines the answer: the crisp skin of roast pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp roasted pork rind accompanies a roast pork dinner, so the description fits it.

clue.text: Dance commercial always presented by singer

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
an ad is a commercial or advertisement
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A singer keeps putting on a dance advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is a poetic shortening of 'ever', which means always.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a singer of ballads, so a performer of songs.

clue.text: Travel free to the Orient

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Free travel to the Far East is on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey on a horse, bike or vehicle is to travel.

clue.text: Self-assertive bishop of impetuous nature

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rash means hasty or impetuous

explanation.surface: A churchman whose impulsive nature makes him pushy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash describes someone loudly confident and pushy, which is self-assertive behaviour.

clue.text: The woman's a goddess

parts.note: her refers to the woman, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A statement that a particular woman is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The woman's a' reads as HER + A: the 's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is queen of the Greek gods and wife of Zeus, an example of a goddess.

clue.text: Market stall offers profit to hospital

parts.note: boot is an old word for profit or advantage, surviving in to boot
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A stall at the market brings in money for the local hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOT as profit is archaic, kept in 'to boot', meaning as an extra benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small stall or stand, as at a fair or market.

clue.text: Make reparation in the early afternoon

definitions.meaning: to make amends for a wrong
split as two words, the phrase means ... o'clock

explanation.surface: Someone makes amends shortly after lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for a wrong is to make reparation; split, it gives at 1 pm.

clue.text: Fellow Frenchman gets job delivering fertiliser

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning fellow, as in co-worker
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A French colleague gets work delivering manure.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed organic matter spread on soil acts as a fertiliser for plants.

clue.text: Oaken growth causes head bitterness

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
gall means bitterness or rancour

explanation.surface: A tree's growth produces a bitter-tasting crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutgall is a gall growing on an oak, caused by insects, so it is an oaken growth.

clue.text: Many a tunic torn apart by madman

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, standing for many

indicators.note: the letters are ripped up and put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A madman rips many a tunic to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn apart' rearranges A TUNIC into UNATIC, after L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic is an old word for an insane person, so a synonym for madman.

clue.text: Bell has made a bloomer

definitions.meaning: something that clangs, such as a bell
British slang for an embarrassing blunder

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer has made an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer and a clanger are both British slang for a blunder; the other sense is literal, a thing that clangs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a ringing bell literally and, in British slang, a howler or blunder.

clue.text: Expired after tin became crystallised

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other, so the tin comes first

parts.note: a can is a tin
expired means died

explanation.surface: Something died after the tin turned crystalline.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied fruit is coated or preserved in sugar, which crystallises around it.

clue.text: To ring and ring us is cruel

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
O is round like a ring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Phoning us over and over is unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'ring's do different jobs: one is to phone, the other the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous means unfeeling and insensitive, so it describes cruel behaviour.

clue.text: Mean to approach

explanation.surface: A miser goes up to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stingy in old use and also to draw close, two dictionary senses.

clue.text: Sortie made by Christian soldiers?

definitions.meaning: a sudden charge out from a besieged position
the ... Army is a nickname for the Salvation Army

explanation.surface: Christian soldiers make a sudden attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The Salvation Army, a Christian charity organised like an army, is nicknamed the Sally Army in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sortie by troops, and the nickname of the Salvation Army's Christian soldiers.

clue.text: Italian family held in the highest esteem

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: An Italian family that is greatly respected.
explanation.definitionFit: The Este were a noble Italian dynasty who ruled Ferrara and Modena.

clue.text: Left one member feeling lethargic

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost a limb is feeling listless.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means drooping and lacking energy, so a synonym for lethargic.

clue.text: Utterly filthy place, an eyesore

indicators.note: utterly is read as when uttered, so the word is spoken

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a filthy place

explanation.surface: A thoroughly dirty place is an ugly sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like an intensifier but means 'when uttered': STY spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Soon enough, everyone's tempo is correct

parts.note: all means everyone; the 's is a link
a musician whose tempo is correct is playing in good time

explanation.surface: Before long, everybody is keeping to the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means eventually, when the right moment comes, so it is a synonym of soon enough.

clue.text: Did the ironing after work when downtrodden

indicators.note: after places the ironing piece behind the work piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Someone irons after work, feeling put-upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oppressed means being kept down harshly, which is what downtrodden describes.
